sources.citation: Keegan, John M. 2014. The Central Sara Languages (Sara Language Project). 9th ed. Cuenca: Morkeg Books. 505 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Transcription for the Sara Languages' section (pp. 6-15) covers consonants, vowels, vowel length and tone ('All of the Sara Languages have three even tones: high, mid and low', p.10) plus Bebote/Nangnda-specific vowel notes; the words stress/accent (prosodic sense) do not occur anywhere in the 505 pages.

sources.access_detail: open link recorded by Glottolog or the catalog, not checked; access check: not located online or in the libraries checked; the linked copy was not accessible when a reader tried
sources.note: The only full phonology of Bedjond (consonants, vowels with instrumental phonetics, syllable structure, vowel quantity, tone; theses.fr subject headings include Prosodie and Ton). If any statement on accent/stress vs tone exists for this language it is here. Hammarstrom/MPI-EVA hold a scan; ANRT microfiche in French university libraries (SUDOC).
